clean_body: Do not share this: A private plea | | | | | | Peter, I just returned home from a week of agonizing meetings with Republican leadership, and I honestly have nowhere else to turn but to you. The things I heard in DC and back here in the state are too difficult to share publicly, but I wrote a special, private note for you— and for you only —detailing the crushing reality. The liberals are pouring millions into their campaigns, and I'm losing sleep knowing that if we fail to hold our seats, we fail President Trump. I'm not supposed to tell you how bad the deficit is, but I can't look away from the truth. Please, I'm humbling myself before you, asking you to read my confidential note immediately. You are my only hope to fight back against this tidal wave of liberal money. And please, promise me you won't share this. If this note gets out, President Trump's fight is over. Forever Humbled, I didn’t run for Senate to sit quietly on the sidelines. I’m a mom, a conservative, and a proud Alabamian—and I came to fight for the values that make America strong. Faith. Family. Freedom. The Left is doing everything they can to tear it all down. But I didn’t come to Washington to play games. I came to fight for the people who feel forgotten, overlooked, and ignored. From securing the border to protecting our kids and defending our way of life—I’m in this for the long haul. This fight isn’t easy, but it’s worth it. And I’m not going anywhere. Will you stand with me? Paid for by Britt for Alabama, Inc.

name: Pramila Jayapal
subject: Wealth inequality is a policy choice
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Pramila for Congress
body:
After the SpaceX IPO, Elon Musk is now worth over $1.1 trillion.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20260612-6348-footer&t=1&akid=6348%2E420207%2E3OTpmZ)
Peter,
**Elon Musk just became the world’s first _trillionaire_**. After the SpaceX IPO, he’s now worth over $1.1 trillion.
$1.1 TRILLION. It's a number so staggering that our brains aren't wired to intuitively understand it.
And it’s happening at a time when 76% of Americans say the cost of living is their biggest economic concern, with 65% saying a middle-class lifestyle is out of reach and 77% saying it’s harder to achieve than a decade ago.
In 49 states, the average renter’s wage isn’t enough to afford a two-bedroom apartment. In 37 states, it’s not even enough for a one-bedroom.
And as of this spring, inflation has outpaced wage growth over the previous 12 months — **meaning workers’ paychecks actually are losing ground.**
Meanwhile, one man is accumulating wealth faster than any human being in the history of the world. And it isn’t an accident.
**It’s a policy choice made by politicians who are more interested in protecting billionaires than fighting for working people.**
They implement policies that let the ultra-wealthy pay lower tax rates than nurses and teachers, creating a rigged system that funnels more and more to the top while the rest of us fall further behind.
**I refuse to accept this.** It’s why I’ve been pushing for policies like a wealth tax, a federal living wage, and Medicare for All—because working people deserve more than scraps.
But Peter, I’m going to be honest with you.
The forces standing in the way of a progressive agenda that puts working people first are powerful. The same billionaires (and now a trillionaire) who are getting richer by the minute are spending huge sums of money to prop up Trump and his MAGA allies, and take down progressive voices in Congress who dare to fight back.
That means I’m going to need your help to take them on. I don’t take money from corporate PACs or lobbyists, and I don’t have billionaires on speed dial. My average online contribution this year is just $27.16.
[**So I’m asking you directly: Will you chip in $27.16 today to help me keep building this people-powered movement and fight for an economy that works for ALL of us, not just those at the top?**](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/53804?c0=pj-em-20260612.W3hRtZ&refcode=em20260612-6348&t=2&akid=6348%2E420207%2E3OTpmZ)

In solidarity,
Pramila Jayapal

name: AOC
subject: Our responsibility is to take care of people.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
#
Our responsibility in Congress is to take care of people.
So before we spend billions of dollars building data centers across the country, **we need to meet some basic protections for people**.
We need some guarantees on our water, and the air we breathe.
We need to make sure that there's a plan for the jobs that stand to be wiped out, so we're not leaving people out to dry.
We should be starting congressional investigations into the effects of AI data centers, and figuring out — with precision — how we protect our water supplies, our power bills, and keep people from getting sick.
The AI lobby has spent billions to become part of our daily lives. [Take a moment to fill out our brief survey about AI today.](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/survey/2026-ai-data-center-moratorium-survey-2/?source=em20260612-11693-P_FND_EGR_GRM&t=3&akid=11693%2E2526796%2EKfUFGA)
**[Take the survey now →](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/survey/2026-ai-data-center-moratorium-survey-2/?source=em20260612-11693-P_FND_EGR_GRM&t=4&akid=11693%2E2526796%2EKfUFGA)**
I know as a politician these companies are going to spend a billion dollars against me for saying it, but **politicians — especially Democrats — should pledge not to take AI money**. 🤷🏻♀️
I refuse all corporate lobbyist money and I don’t believe we should be bankrolled by special interests at all. Each cycle the big dark money interests rotate - NRA, AIPAC, fossil fuel lobby, etc. **This cycle it’s the AI lobby**.
[Help us continue the fight by making a grassroots contribution today.](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/37587?refcode=em20260612-11693-P_FND_EGR_GRM&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=5&akid=11693%2E2526796%2EKfUFGA)
**[Contribute](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/37587?refcode=em20260612-11693-P_FND_EGR_GRM&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=6&akid=11693%2E2526796%2EKfUFGA)**
In solidarity,
Alexandria

**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[The election analyst Newt Gingrich trusts has a word for 2020, and it isn’t “stolen”](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY JEN SCHUMANN, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
Stolen is the wrong word.
Seth Keshel says so himself. And Keshel is a retired Army intelligence captain who has spent nearly six years tagged in headlines as an election denier and a conspiracy theorist. Ask him the obvious question—was the 2020 election stolen—and he says no. He says something else.
“I don’t believe the elections are stolen. I believe that they’re rigged,” Keshel said. “And that’s what Newt Gingrich believes too.”
Keshel, a former Army captain of military intelligence and Afghanistan veteran, built a second career reading election returns the way he once read a battlefield.

**[Eleven Colorado lawmakers on the ballot first reached office through appointment](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY JEN SCHUMANN, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* **Vacancy committees, not voters, decided who represents these districts:** one lawmaker, Jamie Jackson, was appointed to a House seat with just 10 votes from a 19-member committee, while a 2024 Colorado Politics analysis found nearly a third of the entire 100-seat legislature first arrived via appointment rather than election.
* **Some vacancies were created by lawmakers cashing in or stepping away shortly after winning reelection:** Chris Hansen resigned just nine weeks after voters returned him to the Senate to take a $500,000 utility job, and Janet Buckner left weeks after a 45,000-vote win, with replacements chosen by committee votes of 61-37 and 35-of-42 respectively.
* **Even when committees fumble the process, voters rarely get the final say:** one Senate seat was filled by Gov. Polis himself after a vacancy committee missed its paperwork deadline, and historically appointees have lost a primary challenge only a handful of times in 25 years — though five of these 11 face opponents on the June 30 ballot.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**

By the time he walked out, Lorenzo Sewell had given his life to Christ. That same day he went to his drug boss and quit._

Now they’re holding their fourth summit, and this year’s program includes discussions on geothermal energy, data centers, critical minerals, electric cooperative power supplies, workforce development and Colorado River issues._
**[Colorado grew on a wave. The wave is gone.](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** **BY SHAINA COLE | STATE | JUNE 9** _Colorado crossed six million people in 2025, according to the U.S. Census Bureau. _You're getting this message because you’ve supported good causes and Democratic candidates. We need your support to continue fighting for our democracy. We love having you in our network, but if you only want our most important email updates,[click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/108?t=2&akid=2474%2E259176%2EdE-6zV) If you'd like to unsubscribe, [click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/109?t=3&akid=2474%2E259176%2EdE-6zV)_

[](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/11115?source=LOC_EM_FR_2026.06.12_Sand-Gut_B5_F1_S1_C1_90AC-365DON_N-T1&t=4&akid=2474%2E259176%2EdE-6zV) Politicians famously lie a lot, Peter. Now I love a good practical joke here and there, but I don’t lie. That’s one of the many reasons I consider myself a public servant, NOT a politician. So I want to give you the full, unvarnished truth of how I’m feeling about chances in the toss-up race for Governor of Iowa. **Hang on before I start yapping:** I just got my official opponent, and get this: he’s a Kansan culture warrior backed by _Steve King._ **Game on.** Now that we’re up against Zach Lahn and the partisan machine behind him, **[_will you rush a donation between my campaign and Blue Amp Action to help us maximize the post-primary energy here in Iowa? Every bit counts in a race THIS competitive._](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/11115?source=LOC_EM_FR_2026.06.12_Sand-Gut_B5_F1_S1_C1_90AC-365DON_N-T1&t=5&akid=2474%2E259176%2EdE-6zV)** | [Split a Donation >>](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/11115?source=LOC_EM_FR_2026.06.12_Sand-Gut_B5_F1_S1_C1_90AC-365DON_N-T1&t=6&akid=2474%2E259176%2EdE-6zV)
---
Honestly, the primary results didn’t change my feelings much at all. **My gut and recent polling tell me we have a slight lead, but this governor’s race will probably come down to no more than 10,000 votes.**
I don’t want you to think I’m not confident in our chances. I’m extremely confident, in fact: experts have this race pinned as a toss-up, we have a big tent filled with Iowans from literally every walk of life, we have a provably persuasive message, we’re running several TV ads with great feedback from voters, the list goes on and on.

We are witnessing a cascade of primaries in _Iowa_ , _California_ , _South Carolina_ ...and _**right around the corner, here in Arizona**_. _Early in-person voting will begin and mail-in ballots will be accepted starting June 24_. You and all good Republicans in LD27 will be entrusted with selecting a nominee for state senate who best encapsulates our party and puts the best foot forward for our platform. _**For over a decade, I’ve been a party stalwart in Phoenix, working with the Republican majority to pass good, common sense legislation and doing battle with Katie Hobbs and her cronies**_. More than anyone in Arizona, I have spearheaded the movement for election integrity, ensuring that our vote counting is quick, secure, and transparent. **Since he first announced for president in 2015** and promised to build a wall on our southern border, **I have stood side by side with Donald Trump and his efforts to Make America Great Again**. **I was a co-founder of the Arizona Freedom Caucus** , because I know that the Republican Party means nothing if it does not champion proven conservative solutions and uphold the Constitution of our Founding Fathers. I am a faithful Christian, a patriotic American, and a dutiful Republican, in that order. [**It’s not too late to make a difference for our party: chip in $20 for my state senate campaign**](https://us.list-manage.com/BndmSfqIFV_?e=b78dc6f299&c2id=0224aa72dff2928514ac0b5416ed4e8b), and be ready to cast your vote for Anthony Kern once ballots drop on June 24. Currently, interest payments on the national debt have reached approximately $1 trillion per year . For the first time, the cost of simply "servicing the debt" officially exceeds the entire U.S. military budget.

When interest payments become one of the largest expenses in the federal budget, it can create a "crowding out" effect. This means more tax dollars are used to pay for the past, potentially leaving less for the long-term value of the currency in your pocket.

Lawfare Update: Jack Smith and Federal Judges

[INSIDE JW]

LAWFARE UPDATE: JACK SMITH AND FEDERAL JUDGES

[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=83484&L=38047&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cueW91dHViZS5jb20vd2F0Y2g/dj1SRGZXYkZuTGo2RSZ1dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9QU1qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNEJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnM=&hash=a0da2aab262458c6dc2f9928a6a37e248a6b7fa8e5ccabe5e8b9b59f73f75e02]

JUDICIAL WATCH LAWSUIT PURSUES TRANSPARENCY ON JACK SMITH–JUDGE
MEETINGS

Important questions remain about communications between former Special
Prosecutor Jack Smith’s team and the federal judges involved in
President Trump’s cases. The American people deserve full
transparency regarding these meetings and any discussions.

We filed a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) lawsuit
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=83484&L=38025&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2p3LXYtZG9qLXNtaXRoLWhvd2VsbC1ib2FzYmVyZy1jb21wbGFpbnQtMDIwMjcvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1BTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0QmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycw==&hash=b17a3aabf4bba9fa71853fb68ac678e24dec00b73330164946869404679116b5] against
the U.S. Department of Justice for records concerning meetings between
Smith and members of his team and two Obama-appointed federal judges
who presided over matters involving President Donald Trump (_Judicial
Watch Inc. v. U.S. Department of Justice_
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=83484&L=38025&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2p3LXYtZG9qLXNtaXRoLWhvd2VsbC1ib2FzYmVyZy1jb21wbGFpbnQtMDIwMjcvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1BTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0QmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycw==&hash=b17a3aabf4bba9fa71853fb68ac678e24dec00b73330164946869404679116b5] (No.
1:26-cv-02027)).

We sued after the Justice Department failed to respond to a March 24,
2026, FOIA request submitted to the Office of Information Policy (OIP)
for all records concerning meetings between Smith and/or members of
his team and Chief Judge Beryl Howell
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=83484&L=38027&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZGNkLnVzY291cnRzLmdvdi9jb250ZW50L3Nlbmlvci1qdWRnZS1iZXJ5bC1ob3dlbGw/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUFNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJz&hash=6b190f4aa4cefe806a7bd4791654517db6b2ca2d3b54908c50e589aadab6a90b] or
Judge James Boasberg
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=83484&L=38028&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZGNkLnVzY291cnRzLmdvdi9jb250ZW50L2NoaWVmLWp1ZGdlLWphbWVzLWUtYm9hc2Jlcmc/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUFNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJz&hash=7343bf752e1fb6a5c5dce1dddaa8034677a5065b12a477bc4ddaa9ffec68b243]
from December 2022 through April 2023, including notes, recordings,
transcripts, calendar entries, agendas, presentations, and other
related documents.

On November 18, 2022, three days
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=83484&L=29370&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cucmV1dGVycy5jb20vd29ybGQvdXMvdXMtanVzdGljZS1kZXBhcnRtZW50LWFwcG9pbnRzLXNwZWNpYWwtcHJvc2VjdXRvci10cnVtcC1wcm9iZXMtMjAyMi0xMS0xOC8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUFNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJz&hash=ddba73375cd42f2fcc262ee90de1883f8fddb9198f5985bf4a2a4146b16ffa01]
after Trump announced he would run for president again in 2024, former
Attorney General Merrick Garland appointed Special Counsel Jack Smith
to investigate potential criminal wrongdoing by Trump. The appointment
came nine days after then-President Joe Biden announced his effort to
make sure
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=83484&L=38030&F=T&&hash=309b6ab08772dec81be0b0cbf99ac6ca7cb781e61057be0be899b043bca50a89]
Trump did not become president again.

In March 2026, Sen. Chuck Grassley (R-IA) released briefing notes
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=83484&L=38031&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZ3Jhc3NsZXkuc2VuYXRlLmdvdi9pbW8vbWVkaWEvZG9jL2FyY3RpY19mcm9zdF8tX2FnX2JyaWVmaW5nX2Rval9lbWFpbHNfa3Bfc3VicG9lbmFzX25kb3MucGRmP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1BTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0QmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycw==&hash=b1cc44eaf6afd7d1f612f15f0ac76ea86d0097016b2216bcd807e7408ac02238]
prepared for Garland from January 2023 that refer to interactions
between Smith’s team and Judges Howell and Boasberg. The notes
describe a meeting with Howell in which Smith’s team discussed the
pace of the investigation over the preceding month and state that
Howell “liked our approach of pursuing the executive privilege
litigation in an omnibus fashion.” The briefing notes also state
that, regarding a planned omnibus executive privilege motion involving
former Trump administration officials, “Chief Judge knows it is
coming and loves idea.”

The notes also reference “Judge Boasberg = March 18.” Boasberg
became chief judge
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=83484&L=38032&F=T&&hash=6ef79c77f073fe9c9fec33a86b43ec1cf8fe657feea5ce8cde8ffec17e31cb75]
of the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia on March 17,
2023
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=83484&L=38028&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZGNkLnVzY291cnRzLmdvdi9jb250ZW50L2NoaWVmLWp1ZGdlLWphbWVzLWUtYm9hc2Jlcmc/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUFNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJz&hash=7343bf752e1fb6a5c5dce1dddaa8034677a5065b12a477bc4ddaa9ffec68b243],
succeeding Howell and assuming responsibility for supervising grand
jury matters before the court.

Before his appointment to investigate and prosecute Trump, Smith
previously was at the center of several other controversial issues,
the IRS scandal
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=83484&L=28485&F=T&&hash=7d304403d871da9d079a66ed9ab4db4e2cf362db0486ad344a7df1a16d0ee34a] among
them.

We are a national leader in exposing the lawfare and abuse targeting
Trump and other American citizens.

In April 2026, we sued the Justice Department for records on the Biden
FBI’s search warrants used in the April 2021 raid on former New York
City Mayor Rudy Giuliani’s residence and office (_Judicial Watch
Inc. v. U.S. Department of Justice_
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=83484&L=37561&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2p3LXYtZG9qLWdpdWxpYW5pLWNvbXBsYWludC0wMTE1OC9dXz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9QU1qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNEJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnM=&hash=43e7604896dee6667f3608d818fb09828ad371be158870163d6994a2701c5db0 _(No.
1:26-cv-01158)). Giuliani served as a personal attorney and informal
adviser to President Donald Trump.

In May 2026, we obtained
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=83484&L=37493&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZmJpLW9iamVjdGlvbnMtdG8tbWFyLWEtbGFnby1yYWlkLz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NvbnRlbnQ9QU1qY3dPRGs1TlRRJTNEJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj13ZWVrbHkrdXBkYXRlJnV0bV90ZXJtPW1lbWJlcnM=&hash=50e8856ed601dacbf2baa98c8ef301d38c3f1a8ec2497bfc5a81021d4c585186]
records that revealed the FBI’s concerns about the legal basis for
the 2022 raid of Trump’s Mar-a-Lago home. The records exposed
explicit objections from field agents who warned the Justice
Department that the unprecedented raid on Trump’s home lacked
probable cause.

In March 2026, the Justice Department reported
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=83484&L=37416&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZmJpLXJlY29yZHMtaW4taGlkZGVuLXJvb20vP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1BTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0QmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycw==&hash=5bba4a10a75e210b24271e69bfee1fed3b181009546a8907dbec266454469b13] that the
FBI found about 1.9 million pages of records that are responsive to
our FOIA lawsuit. These documents were reportedly stored in a
“hidden room” at FBI headquarters and were first revealed by
former Deputy Director Dan Bongino (_Judicial Watch v U.S. Department
of Justice_
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=83484&L=36534&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2p3LXYtZG9qLWZiaS1oaWRkZW4tcm9vbS1jb21wbGFpbnQtMDQwNDcvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1BTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0QmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycw==&hash=93811d0f9f5804a35881ffcdd110866fcc7a9c266fa0c002097c9c7e356675b6] (No.
1:25-cv-04047)).

In March 2026, we sued
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=83484&L=37382&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvbm9ybS1laXNlbi1hcmN0aWMtZnJvc3QtcHJvYmUvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1BTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0QmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPXdlZWtseSt1cGRhdGUmdXRtX3Rlcm09bWVtYmVycw==&hash=6a2ebc6d5a6227925e42b0fc6e4355b679c3409da64ead3b6e2e079f30c7750e] the
Justice Department for records from the FBI’s Biden-era “Arctic
Frost” probe, specifically involving the Criminal Division, the
Office of Information Policy, Attorney General Merrick Garland, Deputy
Attorney General Lisa Monaco and Special Counsel Jack Smith’s team
(_Judicial Watch, Inc. v. U.S. Department of Justice_
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=83484&L=37381&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9jdW1lbnRzL2p3LXYtZG9qLWVpc2VuLWNvbXBsYWludC0wMDc0Ni8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUFNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJz&hash=6e865a1dca760dffd903b098c54559633a611ea080b9fd09d8f52cfbf0725a98]

FEDERAL AUDIT EXPOSES DHS 'HONOR SYSTEM' FOR TRACKING MILLIONS OF
ILLEGAL ALIEN PAROLEES

The federal government entrusted national security to an astonishingly
ineffective “honor system” by failing to properly monitor millions
of illegal aliens released into the United States under temporary
parole programs. Our _Corruption Chronicles_ blog reports
[https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=83484&L=38048&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvaG9ub3Itc3lzdGVtLXRyYWNrLXBhcm9sZWQtbWlncmFudHMvXTo/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUFNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJz&hash=bd24c07adc7ef37e53a2efbe99698b3ce1ef595c3077520035c535194b915b4a

> In a significant security lapse that has occurred under both
> Democratic and Republican administrations, the government failed to
> track millions of illegal aliens admitted into the United States
> under a temporary parole because the Department of Homeland Security
> (DHS) agency that processed the migrants failed to provide
> identifying information to the DHS agency responsible for monitoring
> them. The unbelievable breach involves Customs and Border Protection
> (CBP), the 60,000-employee frontline border agency charged with
> keeping terrorists and their weapons out of the U.S. and Immigration
> and Customs Enforcement (ICE), the premier federal law enforcement
> agency of around 20,000 that preserves national security and public
> safety by enforcing immigration laws. In a shameful admission
> ICE’s Enforcement and Removal Operations (ERO) reveals that it
> relies on the “honor system” to ensure parolees in the country
> illegally report to field offices as directed, according to a
> scathing federal audit
> [https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=83484&L=38035&F=T&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZ2FvLmdvdi9hc3NldHMvZ2FvLTI2LTEwNzc2NS5wZGY/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUFNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249d2Vla2x5K3VwZGF0ZSZ1dG1fdGVybT1tZW1iZXJz&hash=49e6a20e105f129ff694220f520f8b15877d297c1b0a3f629ce18b370be70dd2].
>
> The probe was conducted by the Government Accountability Office
> (GAO), the investigative arm of Congress, and reveals that from
> October 2018 through May 2025, CBP granted around 2.4 million
> illegal aliens humanitarian parole, many with criminal records and
> over half of them from Mexico, Cuba, and Venezuela. The agency
> expanded the use of the temporary humanitarian measure to mitigate a
> huge increase of migrants crossing into the U.S. along the southwest
> border, which amounted to around 10.4 million during the period
> examined. A few months into the Biden presidency, CBP authorized
> agents to parole apprehended migrants on a case-by-case basis under
> certain conditions, such as limited immigration detention space,
> which was pervasive. A few years later the Biden administration
> greatly expanded access to illegal migration with a special mobile
> application called CBP One that rewarded nearly all
> applicants—97%—parole, the GAO found. “Once noncitizens are
> paroled at the southwest border, U.S. Immigration and Customs
> Enforcement (ICE) is responsible for monitoring them to ensure they
> adhere to the conditions of their release,” the report states.
>
> In fact, last year DHS and ICE issued guidance that emphasized the
> importance of ICE reviewing parole cases to determine whether
> further enforcement action is appropriate. The problem is the
> immigration enforcement agency does not have the information it
> needs to readily identify the illegal aliens that CBP paroled at the
> border. Sounds like a joke, but it is yet another example of
> government inefficiency, of how individual federal agencies fail to
> communicate even when national security, and most likely public
> safety, is at stake. Congressional investigators confirm that ICE
> ERO “is not conducting its required monitoring of all noncitizens
> CBP paroled at the southwest border” and that the laughable
> “honor system” it relies on is clearly not efficient because not
> all paroled migrants report at least once a year as required. In
> 2024 alone ICE lost track of a starling 70% of illegal immigrants
> paroled by CBP and it is not clear what efforts are being made to
> track them down in communities throughout the U.S.
>
> The good news is that illegal immigration is at a historic low under
> President Trump and last spring the administration directed DHS to
> review cases of paroled migrants and terminate the temporary
> reprieve of approximately 654,000. Tracking them down remains a
> problem, the GAO found, because the agency that enforces the measure
> still does not know where the offenders are. “Although DHS and ICE
> guidance emphasizes the importance of ICE’s monitoring and
> enforcement efforts for paroled noncitizens, ICE is not
> well-positioned to carry out these responsibilities because it does
> not have readily accessible information about noncitizens’ parole
> status,” the report states. “According to ICE officials, while
> ICE obtains information from CBP on noncitizens it places in removal
> proceedings, this information does not include the parole status of
> noncitizens who should be monitored, including those whose parole
> was terminated by CBP through the April 2025 notices.”
> Congressional investigators point out that, while CBP systems have
> data fields that provide readily accessible information about parole
> status, officials at ICE’s ERO headquarters maintain its internal
> systems do not have those specific data fields and therefore the
> agency has no access to the critical information.

clean_body: Lawfare Update: Jack Smith and Federal Judges [INSIDE JW] LAWFARE UPDATE: JACK SMITH AND FEDERAL JUDGES [] JUDICIAL WATCH LAWSUIT PURSUES TRANSPARENCY ON JACK SMITH–JUDGE MEETINGS Important questions remain about communications between former Special Prosecutor Jack Smith’s team and the federal judges involved in President Trump’s cases. The American people deserve full transparency regarding these meetings and any discussions. We filed a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) lawsuit [] against the U.S. Department of Justice for records concerning meetings between Smith and members of his team and two Obama-appointed federal judges who presided over matters involving President Donald Trump (Judicial Watch Inc. v. U.S. Department of Justice [] (No. 1:26-cv-02027)). We sued after the Justice Department failed to respond to a March 24, 2026, FOIA request submitted to the Office of Information Policy (OIP) for all records concerning meetings between Smith and/or members of his team and Chief Judge Beryl Howell [] or Judge James Boasberg [] from December 2022 through April 2023, including notes, recordings, transcripts, calendar entries, agendas, presentations, and other related documents. On November 18, 2022, three days [] after Trump announced he would run for president again in 2024, former Attorney General Merrick Garland appointed Special Counsel Jack Smith to investigate potential criminal wrongdoing by Trump. The appointment came nine days after then-President Joe Biden announced his effort to make sure [] Trump did not become president again. In March 2026, Sen. Chuck Grassley (R-IA) released briefing notes [] prepared for Garland from January 2023 that refer to interactions between Smith’s team and Judges Howell and Boasberg. The notes describe a meeting with Howell in which Smith’s team discussed the pace of the investigation over the preceding month and state that Howell “liked our approach of pursuing the executive privilege litigation in an omnibus fashion.” The briefing notes also state that, regarding a planned omnibus executive privilege motion involving former Trump administration officials, “Chief Judge knows it is coming and loves idea.” The notes also reference “Judge Boasberg = March 18.” Boasberg became chief judge [] of the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia on March 17, 2023 [], succeeding Howell and assuming responsibility for supervising grand jury matters before the court. Before his appointment to investigate and prosecute Trump, Smith previously was at the center of several other controversial issues, the IRS scandal [] among them. We are a national leader in exposing the lawfare and abuse targeting Trump and other American citizens. In April 2026, we sued the Justice Department for records on the Biden FBI’s search warrants used in the April 2021 raid on former New York City Mayor Rudy Giuliani’s residence and office (Judicial Watch Inc. v. U.S. Department of Justice [ (No. 1:26-cv-01158)). Giuliani served as a personal attorney and informal adviser to President Donald Trump. In May 2026, we obtained [] records that revealed the FBI’s concerns about the legal basis for the 2022 raid of Trump’s Mar-a-Lago home. The records exposed explicit objections from field agents who warned the Justice Department that the unprecedented raid on Trump’s home lacked probable cause. In March 2026, the Justice Department reported [] that the FBI found about 1.9 million pages of records that are responsive to our FOIA lawsuit. These documents were reportedly stored in a “hidden room” at FBI headquarters and were first revealed by former Deputy Director Dan Bongino (Judicial Watch v U.S. Department of Justice [] (No. 1:25-cv-04047)). In March 2026, we sued [] the Justice Department for records from the FBI’s Biden-era “Arctic Frost” probe, specifically involving the Criminal Division, the Office of Information Policy, Attorney General Merrick Garland, Deputy Attorney General Lisa Monaco and Special Counsel Jack Smith’s team (Judicial Watch, Inc. v. U.S. Department of Justice [] (No. 1:26-cv-00746)). In March 2026, we asked a Georgia state court to reject [] Fulton County District Attorney Fani Willis’ efforts to continue hiding records about her office’s communications with Jack Smith’s office and the January 6 Committee (Judicial Watch Inc. v. Fani Willis et al. [ (No. 24-CV-002805)). In February 2026, we secured the release [] of rosters identifying the names of top deputieS [] who worked for former Special Counsel Jack Smith (Judicial Watch Inc. v U.S. Department of Justice [] (No. 1:23-cv-01485)). In January 2026, we sued [] the Justice Department for communications of FBI agents regarding the prosecution of former Trump trade advisor Peter Navarro (Judicial Watch Inc. v. U.S. Department of Justice [] (No.1:26-cv-00079)). In January 2025, a federal court ordered [] the Justice Department to provide us information on communications between Jack Smith and Fani Willis regarding the prosecution of Trump. In May 2025, the Justice Department was directed to search text messages from the Special Counsel’s Office for responsive records (Judicial Watch v. U.S. Department of Justice [] (No. 23-cv-03110). Congressional investigators confirm that ICE ERO “is not conducting its required monitoring of all noncitizens CBP paroled at the southwest border” and that the laughable “honor system” it relies on is clearly not efficient because not all paroled migrants report at least once a year as required. In 2024 alone ICE lost track of a starling 70% of illegal immigrants paroled by CBP and it is not clear what efforts are being made to track them down in communities throughout the U.S. The good news is that illegal immigration is at a historic low under President Trump and last spring the administration directed DHS to review cases of paroled migrants and terminate the temporary reprieve of approximately 654,000. Tracking them down remains a problem, the GAO found, because the agency that enforces the measure still does not know where the offenders are. “Although DHS and ICE guidance emphasizes the importance of ICE’s monitoring and enforcement efforts for paroled noncitizens, ICE is not well-positioned to carry out these responsibilities because it does not have readily accessible information about noncitizens’ parole status,” the report states. “According to ICE officials, while ICE obtains information from CBP on noncitizens it places in removal proceedings, this information does not include the parole status of noncitizens who should be monitored, including those whose parole was terminated by CBP through the April 2025 notices.” Congressional investigators point out that, while CBP systems have data fields that provide readily accessible information about parole status, officials at ICE’s ERO headquarters maintain its internal systems do not have those specific data fields and therefore the agency has no access to the critical information. name: Defenders of Wildlife
subject: Wildlife Wins: This wolf is making history
body:
Positive news about our wild world, delivered straight to your inbox!

Positive news about our wild world, delivered straight to your inbox!
                  

                  

(https://support.defenders.org/s/5626181/38SyG9Xl)

Dear Defender,

Incredible things are happening in the world of conservation every day, thanks to dedicated people and their supporters. Each month, we’ll bring you uplifting stories about wildlife and wild places!

 

A Big Win for Giant Manta Rays

Called “angels of the sea,” giant manta rays are elegant and massive, which makes them a huge target for aquariums. However, these rays are also listed as threatened under the Endangered Species Act. Despite their vulnerability, until recently Florida has granted permits to capture and ship these rays, sometimes even thousands of miles from Florida’s waters.

Now thanks to public outcry about the dangers to rays, Florida will no longer allow permits to capture them without a full review and vote (https://support.defenders.org/s/5626182/38SyG9Xl), and rays will no longer be shipped long distances to overseas aquariums. This is a huge step toward protecting giant manta rays and Florida’s oceanic waters!

Gray Wolf Enters Sequoia National Park for the First Time in Over a Century

A gray wolf recently traveled hundreds of miles into Sequoia National Park. Her appearance is the first time these wolves have been spotted in the area in over a century. (https://support.defenders.org/s/5626183/38SyG9Xl) Known as BEY03f, her incredible historic journey has been tracked by scientists, conservationists and fans of wolves. This same wolf made headlines earlier this year as the first gray wolf to cross into Los Angeles County since wolves reentered California in 2011.

World’s Largest Wildlife Crossing Coming to California

Wildlife crossings help animals on the move by connecting habitat split up by roads and other development. Six new wildlife crossings are being built in Southern California (https://support.defenders.org/s/5626184/38SyG9Xl), including the largest crossing in the world! Soon, animals like mountain lions, black bears and more will be able move safely through their habitat.

Defenders’ Conflict-Reducing Electric Fence Program Hits Its 15th Year!

As part of our longstanding history of working with landowners and other stakeholders to reduce wildlife conflicts, Defenders launched our Electric Fence Incentive Program. Now in its 15th year, this program stands as one of our most successful coexistence initiatives, avoiding lethal outcomes for bears and other animals. We’re proud to provide communities with the tools and knowledge to share the landscape with our incredible wildlife!

Defenders relies on members like you power ongoing conservation efforts nationwide. Learn how you can lend your support and make a difference with us! (https://support.defenders.org/s/5626185/38SyG9Xl)

(http://www.facebook.com/DefendersofWildlife) (http://twitter.com/defenders) (https://www.instagram.com/defendersofwildlife/?hl=en) (http://www.youtube.com/defendersofwildlife) (https://www.tiktok.com/@defendersofwildlife)

## US, Iran Agree on Peace Deal Text
The U.S. and Iran have reached a [final peace deal text](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0D1u6zAQBODTUB0Naknrp2DxGnV-bUphLa6sTShSIDd2fPvAKXKB1APM4Ju3y3xBjpxu_3EnL2ueEz1qJBEqMxdMeCtEOyV55BJDXblUkRkMdNp0urVzQI7P2TXBr0RAtiHf9kNr3dm2XbP50Y3Dch2uIzobegfOLWEMyzAOeCVCbNi_2kzX2taYwbpT55YODazW9TZgH5QzFFhyOb1nTrLRGp_5TuW05L2JfhM5qrL_FEwKJtlo4xhfmYLpyJGXp4KJk1BJKJwTRgXTeQQw5qwP_OAqmPRn1S-uPggX0oEwaqEv0b9-BVNTfDgeHCPXrlfO3Hbkn6VG_nTd3cN3AAAA__9nh4RU), the strongest signal yet that the war may be ending, Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif announced Friday. A senior Trump administration official said the [agreement could be signed](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFutDAQhJ_GdCDb67PvChd_Q3d_mxIZvMAmxiB7c-jePiKvkGaakb7RfB_P4RkoUV7-hw09z_uQ8awJmbEMVEIOS0HcMPO5lxTrTKUyD1pq20rbKhhioPQeTBP9jKgRGvTK3RWYGyjbrH6CUVpzG60E91DjXU7moR2Cs4CIEBryF01aBUrKO5jOmskGqWcwDmJwURiJkXgv3edOmVec03t_YemmfWuSX5mPKuCf0L3Q_Xme3ZTH6SqF7i-00L28Qmmh--tTGzGklsv3drRH-KLKIbd1DYXmbuUtNcXH46SUqFonjFy2QOl3jf-k6OX1TwAAAP__hfR5YA) within days, though Iran's foreign ministry cautioned that Tehran hasn't reached "a final conclusion." U.S. officials pushed back on information that has been shared publicly by Iran's media about the contents of the forthcoming deal. President Trump wrote in an angry [Truth Social post](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0Dtu6zAQheHVkJ0NPoakbsHiAoE6pwqQUpiII4sBJQrk2IZ3HzhbSHsO8BX_52W6YC55v77jRpGXOu306IWYqU254Y7XRrTRzo_aSupLbp15Msr4k_InbaeEuTwnkCkuRIaspKjDoC04q71cowuJHNLwtYBWs4c5ofPaqETgXfg3yxxfmvLaaqUGC2cPs0dlFgvBJgxJgKKUubbzd807r7SUZ71TO891kyWuzEcX9r8wozAjtxuvvc4Zy-t_jaAaYXmrO5b00W7bIcx41M5dmFFrH2wAPVgHTlkVQLaYjkcuJXcfBKjrhvmXkvynPvdofgIAAP__r8l32Q) Friday morning that the public reporting about the deal has "NOTHING to do with the terms that were agreed to, in writing." Unconfirmed reports say the memorandum would extend the ceasefire for 60 days, reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and tie sanctions relief to Iranian compliance. Hours earlier, U.S. forces reportedly [shot down two Iranian drones](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2O6yAUBOCnwR0WfxcnBcVt3GXbLa0TOCSssLHgxChvv_IW-wJbjzSjbz5vyw1STtvjA1Z0FMuyYW8ZibAuqcIGj4q44ka91BxaTLURLUooy4XlUi8BUn4vZgguIirUAzo5XaQ2_7S0w9PZK4ZolfFeeLQSpmi01Qj366QuAcOQ3NkmrNRSiIs2ozXeglBRm0kHmAIzAkOiUsevkjZ6YszvcmAdfVmH7J5Ee2P6P1MzU3PvffT3dirOnKk5pwP5aw9A2JiaTxTvUPmrcaqvdec7gkceEDL_1TI1D9WFvaecU7MTM-KxQso_m_Snow6nvgMAAP__3O9-5A) targeting commercial ships in the strait.
## Soaring IPO Makes Elon Musk a Trillionaire
SpaceX broke every record in its [Friday market debut](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2uozAQhZ8GOpB_BpsULrahy7ZbosEMyWyMjWxv2Lz9FfcVbnekI52j7_tzn-_IgePjN-7k6pbmSGcJVCvlmTNGfGSinWI9Uw5r2TiXWmcllOmE6aSeV-TwmaFd3UakSLfkpB2lhkFL0z7dCGBhhHG8LXaQNxgsDsIsktDD4hFadteaMFJLIUYNvQFvUKhNg9Ur2rUBQSvXlPu_iWN90hY-6U2592lvg3vWepRG_2rU1KjpPM8-Lv6iuPpGTcu_wpFKadS0Y35RvVI50NP_jo_UlZr8qzsye-qyj6jhZo1os1uPk0PgYmwD4rEjh-_H-iNNb6e-AgAA__9-7Xx7), capping the biggest IPO in history and making Elon Musk the world's first trillionaire. The rocket and AI company raised roughly $75 billion at $135 per share, nearly three times more than any company in history. The stock opened at $150 under the ticker SPCX and climbed past $169, pushing the company's valuation above $2 trillion. Musk, who owns about 42% of SpaceX and controls roughly 85% of its voting power, saw his [net worth top](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD1y6yAURlcDnTz8CdkFxWvU-bUpNQQu0k0QaODGjnefUbaQ8jvfzCnO2325e8xY1v9-B0epLgWePQMRtAWbL35tADsUetaWY0_YOtGihLKDsIPUS_SYX4vh0SUABZqDk9NVajNqafnmvBeQwhjSKG83AZMQNlk5BRvGdxlG4OhOm7BSSyGu2lysCdYLlbSZdPRTZEZARKrt8lGx0AYpv-oD2iXUnWe3ER2d6X9MzUzNtMGGOZ8fU_NRM4bXiSFspea6nmO8KXm1aoBcy7B_9c-hHz7A90ANc8ZaPDZgaubNxeN5om4nZsS6e_w1c_pTqodTPwEAAP__DFd-VA) an estimated $1.1 trillion. Around 4,400 current and former employees also stand to become millionaires.
## U.S. Soccer Team Scores Opening World Cup Win
The U.S. Men's Soccer Team opened its first World Cup game [with a 4-1 victory](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGu4yAURL8Gd7bgQsAuKLZxl223tIi5JKwwWHATlL9_Sn7hdSONNJpz_l23q4sp5vtfd6ClULaMvSUkwrrF6rK7V8QDM_VSk28h1ka0AQc9cj0KuXkX03tTg7cBEVAOaIWZhVQXKfTwsEIZkLeg-O0G84woxIyLvOCsF8MX7oZoP2tcCyk4n6WatNq14xCkMtI745ni6COVOv0vMdMDQ3qXF9ZpL8eQ7IPobEz-YbAyWHvvE7Yzf0oGayv7jvUTqNQ3g3VjsEbPYFULV9qYmcH6bEemNn4Jx_15juXEjHXsro0n1oA7DdX6s8eUYtOGKX4_XEzfA_Qray8LPwEAAP___6OAag) over Paraguay in front of a roaring American crowd in Los Angeles. The Americans [struck first](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DFywyAQheHToM6ehUUgFRRp1DkpUiQdg8TKJoOEBzZ2fPuMc4V0b17xFf_HyZ9Cymk_v4aNHK_F73RvmZip-lTDHs6VaKOd76Xm2NZUG7NXoMwBzEGijyHlh9dddCuRIuzISTtI1D1K012cHvpxwR5nM_fzOGM_aNAxhCUosDMMXXJPDYxECTCgPhq9mABqRW0xBhuFBoqJSz1-lbTzhdb8KDeqx6VsXXYX5msT-CLUJNT083yFmqa3z_drqdyEmhoH_n4OBaY3oOxopbWjtHrArrp4vaecUzNWaDhvIeU_mf-V4-bUbwAAAP__AXxwxw) in the seventh minute when a Christian Pulisic and Weston McKennie move forced Paraguay's Damian Bobadilla to turn the ball into his own net. American forward Folarin Balogun then took over, scoring twice as the U.S. built a 3-0 first-half lead.

Balogun [completed his brace](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFuwyAQxvGnwVsi7sBgDwxdvKUdOrSbdQrnhAqbCK5J8_aV-wrdPn3Db_h_nOYTpZy2yyutHGQp88aPllmE65wqbXSpzCtv8ig1x7ak2kRm1OgO2h3AzJFSfs62i2FhRjYdB_ADGNsbcN01APLY4wimjzwCINKZaBh1HMl6tEOXwq5pBwa0How9Ont2pHEx1ptIPiqrOSYp9fhV0iZXXvKz3Lkez2XtcriK3JoyLwonhdPP_iqcprfP91up0hROTUi-94Ha9Q6M9c73ztkBNHQ1xNsj5Zya88rqy0op_8nyrxz3gL8BAAD__6yScGE) in first-half stoppage time, the first World Cup brace by a U.S. player since the inaugural tournament in 1930.

The U.S. faces Australia next [on June 19](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L1y6yAQQOGnQZ01_Bl0C4rbqHPalBrMLtYmSHhgbY3fPpPkEdKf-YrzflkukQrtt7e4YeBclx2PXpAZ20It7vHWEDfc-aitQM_UOvOipXYn6U7KLBCpvBY7QMiIGs2AQflJGXs2yg1rAC19Ngkg-xSvk0Ow_7zy1-l89gYnN1D41qRTRkk5GTs6m1yUOhvrDUQPwkoE4trGj0o7r5jLqz6xjaluQwkr870L81_oWej5OI7x0XtN6TcQeu5pRXgUPDGlT-Qu9Pzo285DC3A_qBTqzgsrb1uk8oPyn048g_4KAAD__wzBc8w) in Seattle.

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Maine Democrat Senate nominee Graham Platner has come under heavy fire for his many immoral and vile statements. These include lying about a Nazi tattoo, justifying rape, denigrating American hero Chris Kyle, and making remarks about me. I'm the soldier in the viral combat video whom Platner stated "didn't deserve to live."
Platner and his supporters always fall back on the excuse that Platner suffers from PTSD. Many Americans suffer from PTSD, myself included. The issue isn't PTSD; we should be blaming his elitist background.
Due to Platner's privileged upbringing, I seriously doubt he had to truly face any consequences for his abhorrent behavior. We all know a Graham Platner in our lives. He is the "Do you know who my daddy is?" "I can do whatever I want" type of guy.
Platner's family sent him to elite schools and, as an adult, financed vacations and trips to Europe. His father gave him $200,000 for his house, and his mother is his oyster farming client. They have extended a large safety net, essentially not letting him fail in life or learn the lessons associated with struggle. He has lacked many of the character-building experiences associated with enduring the hardships of life and the struggles that working-class Americans endure on a daily basis.
Graham Platner's behavior is not based upon his diagnosis of PTSD but rather on being coddled in socialite society, where accountability is non-existent. Platner has never experienced the rigors of raising children, providing for a family, stressing about bills, or doing what it takes to be a true man. He has continued to act like an entitled child and shirk any responsibility because he has always had his socialite and elitist family to fall back on.
He has tried to cosplay as part of blue-collar America despite his privileged upbringing. The worlds have clashed, and now America wants accountability, not excuses and not a scapegoat. The finger-pointing toward PTSD is unacceptable. It is a victimhood response and, again, is being used as a blanket excuse for poor character.
Due to the numerous controversies involving Platner, many appear to have occurred online, from his Reddit posts to years spent trolling on an app that has become notorious for attracting adult sexual predators seeking contact with minors.
Yet he calls himself a working man. Working men normally don't have the time, desire, or low character to engage in those behaviors.
I am a combat-wounded veteran, Purple Heart recipient, and come from a blue-collar working-class family. I've failed and struggled numerous times in life. Not once did I ever use PTSD as a scapegoat. It's an insult to everyone who has PTSD: veterans, first responders, sexual assault survivors, and many others.
Like the majority of Americans, I have faced life--a hard life and a life that builds and tests character. Struggle builds character, and Graham Platner and his "Do you know who my daddy is?" upbringing have shielded him from that struggle.
Ask yourself a simple question. Would you want Graham Platner alone with your children? Would you want him alone with your wife? Would you want a man like Graham Platner dating your daughter?
Let's just call it what it is. As a combat veteran who has openly struggled with PTSD myself, this isn't PTSD. This is about a total lack of character. Call it that. Not PTSD, but rather a lack of character and accountability.
Teddy Daniels
**Teddy Daniels is a decorated U.S. Army combat veteran.**

Platner has never experienced the rigors of raising children, providing for a family, stressing about bills, or doing what it takes to be a true man. He has continued to act like an entitled child and shirk any responsibility because he has always had his socialite and elitist family to fall back on. He has tried to cosplay as part of blue-collar America despite his privileged upbringing. The worlds have clashed, and now America wants accountability, not excuses and not a scapegoat. The finger-pointing toward PTSD is unacceptable. It is a victimhood response and, again, is being used as a blanket excuse for poor character. Due to the numerous controversies involving Platner, many appear to have occurred online, from his Reddit posts to years spent trolling on an app that has become notorious for attracting adult sexual predators seeking contact with minors. Yet he calls himself a working man. Working men normally don't have the time, desire, or low character to engage in those behaviors. I am a combat-wounded veteran, Purple Heart recipient, and come from a blue-collar working-class family. I've failed and struggled numerous times in life. Not once did I ever use PTSD as a scapegoat. It's an insult to everyone who has PTSD: veterans, first responders, sexual assault survivors, and many others. Like the majority of Americans, I have faced life--a hard life and a life that builds and tests character. Struggle builds character, and Graham Platner and his "Do you know who my daddy is?" upbringing have shielded him from that struggle. Ask yourself a simple question. Would you want Graham Platner alone with your children? Would you want him alone with your wife? Would you want a man like Graham Platner dating your daughter? Let's just call it what it is. As a combat veteran who has openly struggled with PTSD myself, this isn't PTSD. This is about a total lack of character. Call it that. Not PTSD, but rather a lack of character and accountability. ## Midland Gunman Dead After Standoff
The gunman who killed one person and wounded 10 others in Midland on Friday morning was [found dead](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL3OnTAMQJ8GtqD8NYEhQxe2r2tHZBIDlkK4SgJ89-0rbvsG3Y5kyfY5v7-mL6BIaf0FO7r6vRxTwrtErBXztFOIkMJ6ph1SQAjldeayn2WSXBrGDRNqCkDxPek2uJmHQbTohO2F0v2PgbebA7To0Qy6X7yAxWtuhJGKh8EaJYxpyT3LuBFKCK647aziXCx2FlrOVknTaI6B6pG7umHFbyhLfB8X5s4fexvdVuurNOpnI8dGjvd9d2n2j8Uzb-T4YCPHs7B_FBFKZYI9RkwIdpGvtBcGvtKFrGzHUSmtjJKngKmyz1H2NwObIWfyEFj2CZQeet632YXXTTFSMbbRfN2B4ue7-n9NLyf_BAAA___6aYyQ) inside an abandoned veterinary clinic after an hourslong standoff with police. DPS [identified the suspect](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2OgzAQBOCnMR1o_RNMChfX0OXaK5HJLmDJYOR1IHn7U6J7g-tHM_rm5zbcfIhhm7_9Sq48pzRsdHKkUigPa8DoN5wf2-o3JI-8PzKvDx4UqLaGtpZ6QB_iazAVuhHwKity0nZSm-5yhWpxl7scJakJ5USeJrp2gKMxvtPQabL3Krh3GbRSSwkabGM1gJzsKI0arVatMEAYSspNWajQ0_MUX-mg3NzTWkW3lLKz0F9C9UL153k2uHPzCTZzOoTq3yShety5zhTJM3GNVHyIXP8Za15SKmGbq-xwP0OMgVsrDMyrD_GzVP73z-HUbwAAAP__rEd8Ew) as Victor Mata Villarreal, 45, of Odessa, who fired at officers and bystanders along West Wall Street before barricading himself around 8 a.m. He was found dead about 12:30 p.m.; no officers were injured. The Ector County sheriff said Villarreal is the same suspect linked to a [police shooting Wednesday](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2O4yAUBeCnwR0WPw4kBcU27rLtltbF3MRXiyECHJK3H2U0bzD90Tn6zr_rcgWKlO5_YUfXXre8JOw1YmtYlp1ChBTuR9ohBYRQH0ep-1EXJZThwnCplwAU38s0BOdFuMgBnbRnqafz6SKGza0AIRih1lVOXipvDVgfQJ9O3gdvYSD3KRNGaimFFna0Wgh5s15OylutDJsEBmq5jG3Dhi-ot_jOTyzjmvchuq21R2X6D1MzU3PvfXzno3iolD4JpuYPiakZ1kZP5HXLuWHhlPgPkG9YkFPlfYPGO_L_KXem5qG48OgUI1Vj2STuO1D8Xm2_--rp1FcAAAD__6yxgBY). The Texas Rangers are investigating, and Business 20 may stay closed through the weekend.
## GOP Close Ranks in Houston
Texas Republicans [projected a united front](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2urCAUhZ8GOwwbHNGC4jZ2c9tTGhBUEgQDm3Hm7U_GVzjNqr6sv5_n_NQ--Lj914dT-F7THN1VgkN0eT68DTrarcZDR-u0LWfN5ahl5oz3lPUUxGy1D5-5a6wyzI7QOAVyANENj5E1u3rwhYMYFz2sBtZeaq3hYWBY7SJG042NV18z1oMAYILJVgrGYJUGOm6k4D3pmLMeU25xd-jeuqzhk14ut0s6mqB2xLMQ8Y_wifDpuq72hjB7U6NrU94In74ZhE_sKwCETzdDt3TSJcWXi-hTpPesPdWCKVJtTEKkpuacrkJr9PghfGqysuflQ_Cll6Rj26F9uKvg3w58Kf4bAAD__2pGhPA) Friday as Gov. Greg Abbott, Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick, House Speaker Dustin Burrows, and U.S. Senate nominee Ken Paxton addressed the state GOP convention in Houston. Abbott, in a social media post, declared Republicans ["UNITED and ready"](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOhCAURb8GOw08HNCCYhu72XZL85CnkiAYwXHm7zcz2T_Y9ubec5Pzcx_v6IOPyzduZMpzTmOkKwcqhY5x8y5gdMsZN4yO0OX9PPJ25hE4qJqrWsjRoQ-vsa2csdz1oiIjdCdk2916Xq3m1oMUnbW96gkEYKftPE0k0KoZpaPKmzeMKyGF4JLrRkvOxaytaMFqCYq1nJwv6WjKSoWemOfwSg86miltVTBrKXtm8ovBwGC4rquZ0xPUms5cUnyXGAwUaCo-RQbDB1Evaa-nFB8U33F9RkfHha_6b1Ydxu2XD8FnpVnLlw19-ByW_2l6GPgNAAD__xtjfwI) to win in November. Party Chair Abraham George touted [43 legislative priorities](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2SnDAMx5_GdN7xB4GjoEhDd2lTMsKWQYmxGVsst2-fYWfyBNeo-Un6f_z-nD-BIqX1F-w48lfIc8KrRmTGMu_kIyS_nmmH5BF8Pc5S97PORplOqk5qO3ug-Jrbxo-L8oNucNT9h7btx49BNdtolVMDONBmgMGpQbddG7pgcTGDttA3NN7PVKet1sqq_tFbpXToF92apbemE61CT5zLgzdk_IIa4is_sTxc3ps4bsxHFfanMJMw03VdDxfJ_TVbPivndG8JM92xhJne98JMt6Ywk7qH1v-BLHicSyQHqcp8YJKVgVG6nJ6YmHKSR8l_0DGlVZ6J-CUhMBb5QihV5iApBVq3mwszNWX0x0UxUu160ap1B4pv2_y9sp-j-RcAAP__grSVQQ) passed since 2024 but said the failure to close GOP primaries to non-Republicans "must end." One lingering feud eased last week when Secretary of State Jane Nelson, whom the party sued over its closed-primary push, announced she will resign effective July 17. Delegates elect leadership and adopt a platform before the convention wraps today.
## World Cup Lands in Texas Tomorrow
Texas hosts its [first World Cup matches](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDHSpCAQhU-DGVYDCkxAsInZbLqhhdKO1AK6gOPM7bf0Cn_QSXfV1-97f57j0_rg0-u3jWjqZ9nGhGcJWCvmMXoXbHKvI0WbHFpX9iOXeJSRA5cUJGVidNaH79g1zkzgHqxBw5RmotP9A5rV6EX3UswSNPAJFUgQYPtpVmoRoheq8eaCgWSCMRCgWiUA2KIm1vFJCS5JB-h83XJbV6z4sWUJ3-2NuZ232ASz1roXIn4RPhA-nOfZ_q0lXkfCh8uG8GHFjNReEwKtK9Jb4NxycHQ-dhptnVcsdA_2i476RO9HN1IQPvw7sFS_pWvTaw098CYbt58-BF-kIh28ovXhjlR_VuTb8P8BAAD__ywvhZ8) Sunday, when Germany meets Curaçao at noon at Houston's NRG Stadium and the Netherlands faces Japan at 3 p.m. at AT&T Stadium in Arlington. The tournament opened Thursday in Mexico City, where Julian Quiñones scored the Cup's first goal in Mexico's [2-0 win](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLvOnDAQhZ_GdF6NbZZL4SIN3Z82JTKeAawYjHxZ4O0j9hXSjeboHOn7_vyMP8Z5ty-_zUY6X3MYdzqTp5wpjptDb3Zcyr6ZHclgOkpMW0mjBNlwaLhQIxrn77GuUE-AvahIi7YTqu7ePVSrNj1IRJjJzqga2b_fUwd117Vq6mCabeX0MwaNUEKAgvbVKgAxt5Oo5dQq2bAaCF0O8ZVXynSZNPs7fCi-bNgqr9ecj8TULyYHJofzPF-Ujv0JmRxSsJbic-QQbyaHkcnBIZND3YPqoJdPJ0SP3JaDf7lyQHPzyYeFC_lQfr_efYiXA02mxB9JfHZXLpEST3YlLJ54pFR8Tnyjy9nAUyh55X9DJFNFjcfpvHepaVkNy2ac_wLk_9P-0fJfAAAA__8M-pbP) over South Africa. One note of caution: forecasters warn of a [dangerous heat index](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOpDAMhp8GuozsJJuEguKa6fbaK5GHOENOAUaJWXbe_sS9wrb-rE-_vj-f0yflkrfnb1p5lO-0TxufrbAI12nNsdAWn8e20haZYnsdta1HmzRop8ApNFOkXN6T7eP4gDhgzyP6gMaGjwH6ZXQ6uGE2mAZNERgdJ2cD-PQg0Ai2z-MlA4cGEQz4mzcAmPwDrX54o11ngWOWvd5kYeFvaqm89y-ut3lf-zIuIq_WmV-dvnf6fp7n7UxEF-z0narkufAFmGTh2ul7pFKoqbRXUedeZVFUrwayb9eRZ2qi_h4bK7TXQ4lqPl7qSSsrElFNKObjsuvgleOARqNVdoZZWbRBBTck5ckHD2zCB1Jfx_g6cym5Od9ZeK6Uy__58rPoX6P-FwAA___Wz5Py) for Sunday's Arlington match, so hydrate early and often if you're headed out.

# **The 2026 "Trump Effect"
on IRAs over $50,000**
---
**President Trump’s “One Big Beautiful Bill” is exactly what this country needs.** It’s big, it’s bold, and it’s finally putting American families first. But we have to be honest with you about something that’s hard to say. **Trump’s new plan is moving fast** ... maybe too fast for the old, fragile banking system to handle. Think of it like a powerful cleaning crew coming into a dusty old house. They are going to scrub everything clean, which is wonderful. But if you have fragile family heirlooms sitting out on shaky tables... they might get knocked over in the excitement. It’s not Trump’s fault. He is doing his job. **But the Wall Street banks holding your retirement savings are like those shaky tables.** They are old, tired, and not built for this kind of _**Economic Revolution**._ If you leave your money sitting there, it could get caught in the shake-up.
---

# Saturday, June 13, 2026

| This sponsored message from Just The Truth is on behalf of Hillsdale College [](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/v1/c/84NOESJ60yqe8cKuxLM3L3UkMm%2FJlMvy%2Fro5JxMu7SVzsU5Gvnif374%2BK72H%0AbJk4RJ1CGfJroS9nyLOfhKs8DiF2GrNcsSVk3id%2BXft4%2FaNv7GvDGpl%2F5E9C%0AJFqPlTPPmYdY41NIkdq4rTNTyZfeYAX9WOHa%2FXDBTElDRGCX6%2BR3i26IfiUI%0AEyiSJUegezzZjf%2BJ3JP0NoToJkkpXC%2F%2B1w%3D%3D%0A/3eec12d3e51ad49e)Dear Friend,Hillsdale has a video we’d like to share with you today. It’s the trailer for our free online course, “The Second World Wars.”You can watch your video and register for the course below:[**https://info.hillsdale.edu/second-world-wars-sign-up**](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/v1/c/7R2JO9wRHbp5E7Ve90V7O8q1XPrrIytXvhOVTonKtwtyuGCao9MUPKn%2F0fMT%0AaCYu72YWDzdGUwVeH6jnLU21VETNnS8AS%2BI8KcUUZr%2BHOibBBYX4ZIi9ye4C%0APVwYHpZbsdVpfk95oxnmqsPlaDY2ZIHlQRdBMjoCq2BO0Ovi5mAboAAk6NIJ%0AIXf6VsTrfxmUj%2FyCGrcjPmSAJg655KSAMw%3D%3D%0A/bcae0b2be3a8db21)[](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/v1/c/gHSo5ROdcJire2IQXavn2rWMeHaOM%2FRiCVuwfpj6UO%2BhC3%2Bnatn44LZy%2Fpd%2F%0Auzo3mbAt85WDbOknXepjysp2R7lT%2FF%2F2yl1sgGhN0GgUTO%2BC5r3PcpuE7FkK%0AOEkHa6flyW0t7v6t62uMcdTZv8NpTmpaMIBH%2BXPnOLLFwNlx7XA75TiRItWH%0A%2FrKcyqif7GuAkSv43yLLOT81nRBay1yiww%3D%3D%0A/4275ceba76a10c8a) World War II was the most significant armed conflict in human history—fought across continents, oceans, and skies with unprecedented scale and intensity.Yet despite its complexity, this war can be understood.That’s why we created this course, “The Second World Wars.” It organizes the conflict into seven key topics—The Stakes, Air, Water, Earth, Fire, People, and Ends—to give you a clear understanding of how and why the Allies won.In this course, you’ll learn:
* what was at stake for civilization during World War II
* how different theaters of war shaped the outcome
* the strategies and investments of Allied and Axis powers
* the role of leadership, technology, and industrial strength
* how a global conflict became one unified war

To guide this journey, we are pleased to feature Dr. Victor Davis Hanson and Dr. Larry P. Arnn.Together, they bring clarity and depth to one of the most complex events in history—helping you see not just what happened, but why it mattered.[After watching the trailer](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/v1/c/%2FAGSrLiUgv2j7AqrTb5BW7FeDBMJmt2y3EqqN5QbQ4gM4L1SCieojlHSk%2Bs1%0ANdiy3K35TrzGoo%2FyvemMaaIzIF4DOcKeEcKvLRe9TEZlnTONjJkQJQaCSY42%0ATci9TYduBjfQuoAZ5uHRHHf3mhXAbv4WTrGDWwKhjKSDGj1TqhIc6rDYRgd6%0AAAlFKIUW1kpKdnbwMkC1K8tsMXQH7Bownw%3D%3D%0A/9adf5db34c74e5cc), I hope you’ll join us by registering for this free online course. You can do so easily on the same page as the video.Understanding World War II is essential to understanding the modern world—and the preservation of freedom itself.I hope you enjoy your sneak peek.Warm regards,

Bill Gray, ’01
Vice President
Institutional Advancement
Hillsdale College

name: Douglas Carswell
subject: The Six Stages of AI
body:
| | | [View this email in your browser](https://us18.campaign-archive.com/?e=5703353baa&u=60d4052c66b6745831ccdf7c8&id=61ee96fe0e)
---
| |
---
| _**If you're not in front of our Saturday email, you're behind.**_
---
| Dear Friend,
When something new comes along, everyone suddenly has to have an opinion about it. Often the same one.

When crypto went mainstream, people who had never owned so much as a share were suddenly holding forth on bitcoin. When Ozempic arrived, people who had never once expressed a view on weight loss were just as eager to share the very same thoughts. Now it is AI’s turn. No conversation about it seems complete until someone has solemnly used the word “hallucination”.

AI is utterly transformative. A vastly bigger deal than almost any innovation that came before. As big as the invention of writing, or the industrial revolution — only all at once.

Whether you run a business, a club, a school — or a think tank, as I do — it is going to upend a great deal of what we take for granted. Who you hire. How you delegate. What outcomes we should even expect from our employees. It lets you work almost at the speed you can think — fast enough that knowing when to stop becomes a discipline in its own right.

My own journey with AI started where everyone’s does —marveling at how my newly opened account acts as such an awesome search engine. Call it the “Does anyone still use Google anymore?” stage: you put your new tool to work running glorified Google searches. Great fun — but if that is as far as you get, you could be forgiven for thinking the whole thing overhyped.

The second stage of AI is when you start using AI as a writing tool. This is where those who talk about hallucinations tend to be. And it is, frankly, the least interesting thing about AI. Sure, it is excellent for editing and polishing what you have written — but not the other way round, with you editing what it writes. That is the surefire route to slop.

The third is the realization that you can do things techies spent years learning to do. Figure out how to program an agent to perform one complex task, and it can then perform that same task again and again — at a scale, and a speed, no human team could match. (Information and expertise that once belonged only to those at the top of society are coming within reach of everyone else. The social implications of that are at least as large as the economic ones.)

Perhaps my all-time favorite TV show is Young Sheldon. The running joke throughout every episode is that Sheldon, the brilliant boy genius, is able to figure out extraordinary things, yet is forever tripped up by the mundane.
---
|
---
_Young Sheldon – just like dealing with AI?_
| Treat AI as you might Sheldon: super smart, but dumb enough to misread the obvious.

The fourth stage of AI comes when you realize an agent can handle a great deal of your existing workflow. Instead of getting you or your team to do the donkey work, you farm it out to your new AI employee — one who never tires, and shows up on time, every time, ready to put in a full day’s work. (Is your new AI colleague a virtual worker or ubiquitous?)

The fifth stage arrives once you start asking what you might automate that you never imagined could be automated at all. At MCPP we are beginning to do precisely this, in all sorts of weird and wonderful ways.

This week it was reported that AI software built by Palantir has saved hundreds of lives at a hospital in Florida by catching the signs of sepsis before doctors could. No miracle cure: the system simply reads the data already flowing through the hospital and prompts preemptive action.

Now picture the same logic applied more widely. Imagine AI scanning the records of every American over a certain age, picking out each one whose cholesterol sits in the danger zone, and ensuring they are offered statins - a few dollars a day - to bring it down. AI need not conjure something out of nothing to be transformative, but to merely take the knowledge already sitting in front of us, ignored, and put it to work.

The sixth stage of AI follows when you work out how to automate the autonomous agents themselves, so that they more or less manage one another. Ask me how that is going in a few weeks...

So where might all this lead?

I am an optimist. I think Jeff Bezos is right. Far from causing mass unemployment, AI could leave us with a shortage of workers.

Yes, there will be disruption. Anyone who fails to adapt could lose out. It may not be much fun for those whose only skill is coding. But there will also be an enormous increase in output. Every one of us has some sort of comparative advantage, and AI lets us do far more with what we have than ever before.

The result could be far greater prosperity for all — provided we let energy producers produce, rather than strangle them in red tape, and provided we steer well clear of European Union-style control from the top down. (The EU’s GDPR goes a long way to explaining why so much AI innovation is happening on this side of the Atlantic, and so little on the other.)

One final thought. Energy policy is about to matter more than almost anything else. AI runs on power — vast and growing amounts of it — and the states and nations that produce energy cheaply and abundantly are the ones that will get to build the future. Those that hobble their energy producers will be left watching from the sidelines.

clean_body: | | | | | | If you're not in front of our Saturday email, you're behind. | Dear Friend, When something new comes along, everyone suddenly has to have an opinion about it. Often the same one. When crypto went mainstream, people who had never owned so much as a share were suddenly holding forth on bitcoin. When Ozempic arrived, people who had never once expressed a view on weight loss were just as eager to share the very same thoughts. Now it is AI’s turn. No conversation about it seems complete until someone has solemnly used the word “hallucination”. AI is utterly transformative. A vastly bigger deal than almost any innovation that came before. As big as the invention of writing, or the industrial revolution — only all at once. Whether you run a business, a club, a school — or a think tank, as I do — it is going to upend a great deal of what we take for granted. Who you hire. How you delegate. What outcomes we should even expect from our employees. It lets you work almost at the speed you can think — fast enough that knowing when to stop becomes a discipline in its own right. My own journey with AI started where everyone’s does —marveling at how my newly opened account acts as such an awesome search engine. Call it the “Does anyone still use Google anymore?” stage: you put your new tool to work running glorified Google searches. Great fun — but if that is as far as you get, you could be forgiven for thinking the whole thing overhyped. The second stage of AI is when you start using AI as a writing tool. This is where those who talk about hallucinations tend to be. And it is, frankly, the least interesting thing about AI. Sure, it is excellent for editing and polishing what you have written — but not the other way round, with you editing what it writes. That is the surefire route to slop. The third is the realization that you can do things techies spent years learning to do. Figure out how to program an agent to perform one complex task, and it can then perform that same task again and again — at a scale, and a speed, no human team could match. (Information and expertise that once belonged only to those at the top of society are coming within reach of everyone else. The social implications of that are at least as large as the economic ones.) Perhaps my all-time favorite TV show is Young Sheldon. The running joke throughout every episode is that Sheldon, the brilliant boy genius, is able to figure out extraordinary things, yet is forever tripped up by the mundane. | Young Sheldon – just like dealing with AI? | Treat AI as you might Sheldon: super smart, but dumb enough to misread the obvious. The fourth stage of AI comes when you realize an agent can handle a great deal of your existing workflow. Instead of getting you or your team to do the donkey work, you farm it out to your new AI employee — one who never tires, and shows up on time, every time, ready to put in a full day’s work. (Is your new AI colleague a virtual worker or ubiquitous?) The fifth stage arrives once you start asking what you might automate that you never imagined could be automated at all. At MCPP we are beginning to do precisely this, in all sorts of weird and wonderful ways. This week it was reported that AI software built by Palantir has saved hundreds of lives at a hospital in Florida by catching the signs of sepsis before doctors could. No miracle cure: the system simply reads the data already flowing through the hospital and prompts preemptive action. Now picture the same logic applied more widely. Imagine AI scanning the records of every American over a certain age, picking out each one whose cholesterol sits in the danger zone, and ensuring they are offered statins - a few dollars a day - to bring it down. AI need not conjure something out of nothing to be transformative, but to merely take the knowledge already sitting in front of us, ignored, and put it to work. The sixth stage of AI follows when you work out how to automate the autonomous agents themselves, so that they more or less manage one another. Ask me how that is going in a few weeks... So where might all this lead? I am an optimist. I think Jeff Bezos is right. Far from causing mass unemployment, AI could leave us with a shortage of workers. Yes, there will be disruption. Anyone who fails to adapt could lose out. It may not be much fun for those whose only skill is coding. But there will also be an enormous increase in output. Every one of us has some sort of comparative advantage, and AI lets us do far more with what we have than ever before. The result could be far greater prosperity for all — provided we let energy producers produce, rather than strangle them in red tape, and provided we steer well clear of European Union-style control from the top down. (The EU’s GDPR goes a long way to explaining why so much AI innovation is happening on this side of the Atlantic, and so little on the other.) One final thought. Energy policy is about to matter more than almost anything else. AI runs on power — vast and growing amounts of it — and the states and nations that produce energy cheaply and abundantly are the ones that will get to build the future. Those that hobble their energy producers will be left watching from the sidelines. | "Forward this email to a friend!" | | Warm regards, Douglas Carswell President & CEO Mississippi Center for Public Policy | | |

disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY CITIZENS FOR BRAD SMITH**
body:
Nearly 2,000 signatures, major labor endorsements, and a growing grassroots movement across Wisconsin’s 6th District.

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/43a2fc5e902c/officially-on-the-ballot-and-building-momentum-every-day-17459170?e=a4a0e00aa9)
---
| | | | |
---
| |
Hi Peter,

Summer has arrived and the campaign is kicking it into high gear. We have a lot to be proud of so far.**We lead the field in nomination signatures.** In only 10 days, our amazing volunteer network gathered 1917 approved signatures. This number exceeds the amounts submitted by all other candidates, including Glenn Grothman. Brad was only the fifth candidate out of all Wisconsin races to hand in his signatures. We are officially on the primary ballot.**We were endorsed by one of Wisconsin’s largest labor unions.** The Wisconsin Educators Association Council (WEAC) and the National educators Association (NEA) have officially put their support behind Brad. WEAC interviewed all Congressional candidates and evaluated their vision for public education. They selected Brad as the sole endorsed candidate in this race. The endorsement underscores growing support for our campaign across multiple sectors, and especially to the state’s educators. Our campaign has also been endorsed by over [30 local legislators and leaders](https://us.list-manage.com/zUTLx34iRtD?e=a4a0e00aa9&c2id=92e2d37cfd6b9cebafd3106e51945da8) across the District and we are honored to have their confidence!**We continue to lead the field in fundraising.** Our campaign continues to be powered by individual donations, almost exclusively within the District. Brad is not accepting any PAC or corporate dollars, and we have raised over $120,000. Fundraising continues to be a high priority, since resources make it possible to spread the word through advertising, yard signs, text campaigns and literature. As more voters begin to pay attention to this race, it’s critical that we are able to reach them. **There are many ways you can help the campaign grow.**
* **Donate****.** Every dollar donated gets us closer to competing with Glenn’s deep pockets.
* **Attend an event.** And bring some friends! Upcoming opportunities are listed below, and strong attendance sends a strong message.
* **Knock doors.** Canvassing wins races. We are looking for volunteers in all counties who would like to spread the word about Brad. No experience is needed and you can get started right away. Please reply to this email to connect with your county captain.
* **Talk to your neighbors.** Word of mouth is and has always been one of the most effective ways to raise awareness.

We are closing in on 2 months until the August 11th primary election. Every conversation, every day and every dollar matters. Thank you for all you do and your support!Together, we can make this the strongest campaign possible and flip the 6th District this November! 💪
